rubric.why: A hypotonic solution has a lower solute concentration than the solution it is compared with.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that its solute concentration is lower than that of the comparison solution.

rubric.why: A hypertonic solution has a higher solute concentration than the solution it is compared with.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that its solute concentration is higher than that of the comparison solution.

modelAnswer: A hypotonic solution has a lower solute concentration than the solution with which it is compared.
A hypertonic solution has a higher solute concentration than the solution with which it is compared.

items.followUp: Explain how cytokinesis takes place in animal cells.

rubric.why: In plant cells, a cell plate begins to form in the middle of the cell.
rubric.description: States where the cell plate forms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the cell plate forms at the centre or middle of the cell.

rubric.why: The cell plate grows outwards and develops into a new cell wall, separating the two daughter cells.
rubric.description: Explains how the cell plate separates the daughter cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the plate grows or develops into a wall and divides the cytoplasm.

modelAnswer: A cell plate forms in the middle of the plant cell and grows outwards towards the cell membrane.
The cell plate develops into a new cell wall, dividing the cytoplasm into two daughter cells.

items.followUp: Define anabolism and catabolism, and name the scientist who first used the term metabolism.

rubric.why: Metabolism refers to the chemical reactions occurring within cells or an organism.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining metabolism as the chemical reactions taking place within a cell or organism.

rubric.why: The term or concept of metabolism is attributed to Theodor Schwann.
rubric.description: Names the scientist associated with the concept of metabolism.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming Theodor Schwann.

modelAnswer: Metabolism is the sum of all the chemical reactions occurring within the cells of an organism.
Theodor Schwann first gave the concept of metabolism.

items.followUp: What is an enzyme? Explain its role in a metabolic pathway.

rubric.why: A metabolic pathway is an ordered sequence of reactions.
rubric.description: Identifies a metabolic pathway as a sequence of reactions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as a sequence or series of reactions.

rubric.why: The reactions are controlled by enzymes, and the product of one reaction can be the substrate for the next.
rubric.description: Describes enzyme control or the link between successive reactions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that enzymes control the reactions or that one reaction's product enters the next reaction.

modelAnswer: A metabolic pathway is a sequence of chemical reactions occurring in a cell.
Each reaction is controlled by a specific enzyme, and the product of one reaction becomes the substrate for the next.

items.followUp: What are aerobes? Give two examples of anaerobic organisms.

rubric.why: Anaerobes can live or carry out their activities without oxygen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that anaerobes live or function without oxygen.

rubric.why: Yeast and Clostridium are examples of anaerobic organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming two valid examples, such as yeast and Clostridium.

modelAnswer: Anaerobes are organisms that can live and carry out their activities without oxygen.

items.followUp: Name the components of ATP and state its function in cells.

rubric.why: Adenine joined to ribose forms adenosine, the first part of the ATP structure.
rubric.description: Shows the adenosine part of the ATP structure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including adenine and ribose, or identifying them together as adenosine.

rubric.why: ATP has three phosphate groups attached to adenosine.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for showing or naming three phosphate groups attached to adenosine.

modelAnswer: Adenine joined to ribose forms adenosine; three phosphate groups are attached to it.

items.followUp: Explain how humidity affects the rate of transpiration.

rubric.why: Moving air generally increases transpiration by carrying water vapour away from the leaf surface.
rubric.description: States the effect of increased air movement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that increased air movement or wind increases the transpiration rate.

rubric.why: Removing moist air around the leaf maintains a diffusion gradient for water vapour to leave the leaf.
rubric.description: Explains why air movement increases transpiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that moving air removes water vapour or moist air from around the leaf.

modelAnswer: As air movement increases, the rate of transpiration generally increases.
Moving air carries water vapour away from the leaf surface, maintaining a gradient for further water loss.

items.followUp: Name the valves that separate the atria from the ventricles.

rubric.why: The upper chambers of the heart are the right and left atria (auricles).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both the right and left atria, also called auricles.

rubric.why: The lower chambers of the heart are the right and left ventricles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both the right and left ventricles.

modelAnswer: The four chambers of the human heart are the right atrium, left atrium, right ventricle and left ventricle.
